review_notes: I read the whole file. It declares no simp lemmas and no simp attributes. Its simp use is local: `simpa [μ]`, `simp [a, hzero]`, `simp only [...]`. I found no loops, competing rules or unwanted expansion in it. The one interface gap is the plain `def spaceTimeSet`, which has no simp or membership lemma, and I checked that definition and its uses in other files. I did not check how many of the other-file call sites would actually be shortened. I haven't run Lean, so I can't say whether a `mem_spaceTimeSet` simp lemma would change any existing simp call.

findings.excerpt: have hboxset : (spaceTimeSet Ω' J : Set (Vec3 × ℝ)) = Ω' ×ˢ J := rfl
findings.problem: `spaceTimeSet Ω I` is a bare `def` for `Ω ×ˢ I`, defined in Statements/SpaceTimeSet.lean. It has no `mem_spaceTimeSet` lemma, no `spaceTimeSet_eq` equation lemma and no simp attribute. This file rebuilds the equality with `rfl` at line 840. Elsewhere, call sites unfold the definition by hand. Examples are `simpa [B, J, spaceTimeSet] using hbox` and `simp only [goodPointPastCylinder, spaceTimeSet]`. Membership goals such as `z ∉ spaceTimeSet Ω' J` in the `_zero_` lemmas are handled by `change` and defeq casts. Without a simp lemma, simp does not turn a `spaceTimeSet` membership goal into `z.1 ∈ Ω' ∧ z.2 ∈ J`. Callers must pass the definition name to simp each time.
findings.proposed_change: In Statements/SpaceTimeSet.lean, add `theorem mem_spaceTimeSet {Ω I z} : z ∈ spaceTimeSet Ω I ↔ z.1 ∈ Ω ∧ z.2 ∈ I := Iff.rfl` and tag it `@[simp]`. This is a terminating rewrite from an opaque predicate to concrete conditions, so it cannot cycle. Optionally add `theorem spaceTimeSet_eq : spaceTimeSet Ω I = Ω ×ˢ I := rfl`, deliberately not simp, and use it instead of the local `hboxset`. Do not make the equation itself simp unless call sites such as `Measure.prod_restrict` rewrites are checked, because that could change `volume.restrict (spaceTimeSet ..)` terms that other lemmas state in terms of `spaceTimeSet`.
findings.benefit: Callers can write `simp` or `simpa` for set-membership and zero-outside-box goals without adding `spaceTimeSet` to the simp set. The local `rfl` helper `hboxset` and `change`-based coercions become unnecessary. The canonical form for membership is one place, instead of the `[B, J, spaceTimeSet]` unfolding list repeated across files.
